source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 12 iunie — «Sfântul Cuvios Onufrie cel Mare»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Ιουνίου — «Όσιος Ονούφριος ο Αιγύπτιος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and gives no years. It is plainly the same man: the great ascetic of the Egyptian deserts, a Persian by birth, who went deep into the desert, was met by the hermit Hermias and settled under a great palm beside a spring, and died as abba Paphnoutios visited him, who buried him under that palm. The page records portions of his relics at the monastery of his name at Keratea in Attica and at the monastery of Leimonos on Lesbos. It keeps him on the same day as Peter the Athonite and prints one apolytikion naming them both. Its kontakion, «Φῶς νοητὸν καὶ οὐράνιον, Πέτρε», names Peter and not Onuphrius, and is a mis-hang so far as this folder goes: no hymn is taken from it here. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

hymns.text: Dumnezeul părinţilor noştri, Care faci pururea cu noi după blândeţile Tale, nu îndepărta mila Ta de la noi; ci pentru rugăciunile lor, în pace îndreptează viaţa noastră.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Onufrie cel Mare; the page prints the common troparion of venerable fathers, naming no saint in the text.

english.text: O God of our fathers, who dealest with us always according to Thy gentleness, take not Thy mercy from us; but at their prayers guide our life in peace.

hymns.text: Τῶν Ἀγγέλων τὸν βίον ἐν σαρκὶ μιμησάμενοι, ὤφθητε ἐρήμου πολίται, καὶ χαρίτων κειμήλια, Ὀνούφριε Αἰγύπτου καλλονή, καὶ Πέτρε τῶν ἐν Ἄθῳ ὁ φωστήρ· διὰ τοῦτο τοὺς ἀγῶνας ὑμῶν ἀεί, τιμῶμεν ἀναμέλποντες· δόξα τῷ ἐνισχύσαντι ὑμᾶς, δόξα τῷ στεφανώσαντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργούντι δι' ὑμῶν πάσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος α’, Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης — the first of two apolytikia on the page of «Όσιος Ονούφριος ο Αιγύπτιος», and the one that names him with Peter the Athonite; the same hymn stands on Peter's page too

english.text: Having imitated in the flesh the life of the angels, you were shown to be citizens of the desert and treasuries of graces — Onuphrius, the beauty of Egypt, and Peter, the luminary of those on Athos. Therefore we honour your contests always, singing: Glory to him who gave you strength, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who through you works healings for all.

hymns.text: Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης καὶ ἐν σώματι ἄγγελος, καὶ θαυματουργὸς ἀνεδείχθης, θεοφόρε Πατὴρ ἡμῶν Ονούφριε· νηστείᾳ ἀγρυπνίᾳ προσευχῇ, οὐράνια χαρίσματα λαβών, θεραπεύεις τοὺς νοσοῦντας, καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν πίστει προστρεχόντων σοι. Δόξα τῷ δεδωκότι σοι ἰσχύν, δόξα τῷ σὲ στεφανώσαντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργοῦντι διὰ σοῦ πᾶσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος α´, Τοῦ λίθου σφραγισθέντος — the second of two apolytikia on the page of «Όσιος Ονούφριος ο Αιγύπτιος»; it is the common of a venerable father with his name set into it, and names him alone. The page's spelling «Ονούφριε» is unaccented there as printed

english.text: A citizen of the desert, an angel in the body and a wonderworker were you shown to be, our God-bearing father Onuphrius: by fasting, by vigil and by prayer you received heavenly gifts, and you heal the sick and the souls of those who run to you in faith. Glory to him who gave you strength, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who through you works healings for all.
